## Summary

**Search process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront (best_so_far_above 1.2 → stop; failures_at_least 2 → stop; last_gain_at_most 0.03 → restart), and a weak prior favoring simplicity.
- Explored 7 independent anchors (features 32, 33, 18, 16, 19, 38, 14) via `init`/`restart`, extending each with `extend_best`.
- Every path consistently converged to the same best basin: **feature 33 (long) + feature 35 (short)**, Sharpe 0.491 (all-years) / 0.554 (recent-weighted) — while no third feature ever improved on this pair, and all other anchors topped out well below it (0.14–0.46 range).
- When diminishing/negative gains repeatedly fired my restart trigger, I eventually switched it to a stop action (logged via `change_trigger`) once the evidence of convergence was overwhelming, and formally stopped the search.

**Candidate submitted:** rule **[33 long, 35 short]**, a 2-feature equal-weight combination, clearly dominating the baseline model (0.183/0.246 Sharpe, 0.042 turnover).

**Prediction for unseen data:** mean annualized net Sharpe **0.30**, sd **0.25** — a substantial haircut from the in-sample 0.49, reflecting realistic decay expected from a search over 40 candidate features even though this particular combination showed unusually robust convergence across many independent search paths.
